- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3–5% above recent peak unless sentiment shifts.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.33) for 3+ consecutive days, model underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to account for mean reversion.
- Model frequently overreacts to short-term sentiment swings; smooth 3-day moving average of sentiment before adjusting forecast.
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome deviates >3% from 14-day moving average, adjust forecast toward historical mean (last 60 days) if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67), model often fails to capture mean reversion; apply 1–2% downward bias if price has been rising for 5+ days.
